Write a Blocks Sheet's Cells in as Few Calls as Possible

Source: R/format_xlsx.R
ck_write_question_cells.Rd

openxlsx::writeData() costs roughly its column count per call, almost regardless of how many rows it writes: on a 523-column sheet, sixty calls of eleven rows took 2.52 s where one call of the same 31,380 cells took 0.22 s. The blocks layout made two calls per question, so the write was sixty times more expensive than the cells justified.

Usage

ck_write_question_cells(wb, sheet, headers, bodies, n_col, last_row)

Arguments

wb

An openxlsx workbook.

sheet

Sheet name.

headers

A list of list(row, values), one per question: the three header rows as a character matrix.

bodies

A list of list(row, values), one per question: the data rows as a list of one vector per sheet column.

n_col

Number of columns on the sheet.

last_row

The last row the sheet uses.

Value

Invisibly the number of writeData() calls made.

Details

Here the data area of the whole sheet is written once, and only the three header rows of each question are written separately. The order is not interchangeable: writeData() clears every cell of the rectangle it covers, NA included, so the body pass leaves the header rows blank and the header pass fills them afterwards. Writing them the other way round would blank every header.

A column is only batched when every question contributes the same kind of vector to it. If one question put text where another put numbers, stacking them would coerce the numbers to text and Excel would stop treating them as numbers - so a mixed column sends the whole sheet back to the per-question path, which is slower and exactly correct.
